memory_update.text: HMDPF should be tracked as the cleanest public pure-play candidate for dry-type transformers and power-quality equipment, but its OTC U.S. listing and Canadian primary listing may complicate liquidity and U.S.-only mandate eligibility.

POWL is a strong switchgear-adjacent candidate with recent data-center evidence, but its market cap now sits around the edge of the preferred underfollowed range and the key risk is lumpy mega-project concentration.
PLPC is an underfollowed second-order grid hardware supplier; include in future passes only if transmission/distribution hardware demand can be tied to concrete utility T&D capex and order growth.

The node should be split in later layers into: direct transformer/power-quality suppliers, medium-voltage switchgear and packaged electrical systems, transmission/distribution line hardware, and diversified reference leaders.

Need a dedicated search for additional U.S.-listed small/mid-cap suppliers in capacitor banks, reactors, harmonic filters, busway, electrical enclosures, relays, breakers, and testing/inspection services tied to data-center and utility power equipment.

node: Dry-type transformers, distribution transformers, magnetics, power quality, switchgear-adjacent equipment, and low/medium-voltage power distribution
summary: Layer 1B expands the stock universe around transformer, power-quality, and switchgear-adjacent bottlenecks. The underfollowed lane is strongest in Hammond Power Solutions, Powell Industries, and Preformed Line Products: each sits one or two steps away from the obvious AI/data-center power story but may benefit if transformer, switchgear, transmission-hardware, and grid-equipment procurement remain schedule-critical. Hubbell is included as a higher-attention reference anchor because it validates the same utility, substation, distribution, and datacenter electrical-equipment demand pool, though it is less pure.
